FOR THE HARD-TO-BUY-FOR PILOT

They have everything. Now what?

Find something different ›

Our top 10 pilot gift ideas, ranked

How we rank ›

Our editorial order for a broad aviation-gift shortlist: personal appeal first, followed by usefulness and how easy the gift is to get right. A pilot’s exact wishlist should always outrank a general list. These are researched picks, not hands-on test results.

  1. 1
    For the collector

    LEGO Icons Concorde

    Listed price: $199.99 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: An evening project that becomes a permanent part of their aviation corner. A strong choice for someone who loves airliners as much as flying them.

    What to know: Allow a long display shelf: the finished model measures 41.5 inches. Ages 18+.

    Product details & source ↗
  2. 2
    A milestone keepsake

    Cessna 172 Skyhawk model

    Listed price: $249.00 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: The best model is often the aircraft with a story behind it. This mahogany Skyhawk is especially thoughtful for someone who learned to fly a Cessna 172.

    What to know: Confirm their aircraft type. A 172 and a 182 are different airplanes, even if they look similar.

    Product details & source ↗
  3. 3
    For their next flight

    Flight Gear Stealth Bag

    Listed price: $79.95 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A flight bag is a gift they can use beyond the holidays. This compact backpack-style option is worth a look when their current setup is an overflowing ordinary bag.

    What to know: Compare the listed dimensions with their headset, tablet and usual load before choosing.

    Product details & source ↗
  4. 4
    A useful little extra

    Flight Gear Aviator’s Light

    Listed price: $29.95 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A compact light with separate red and white controls. It makes sense for the person who likes keeping small, useful tools in their flight bag.

    What to know: Ask what light they already carry; this is an accessory, not a replacement for required equipment.

    Product details & source ↗
  5. 5
    Under $25

    SKILCRAFT B3 Aviator pen

    Listed price: $24.50 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: Black ink, red ink and a pencil in one everyday tool. An uncomplicated addition to a practical gift bundle, especially with a handwritten note.

    What to know: Check whether they prefer paper notes; an all-digital pilot may get less use from it.

    Product details & source ↗
  6. 6
    For a first lesson

    ASA pilot logbook

    Listed price: $9.49 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: An affordable way to mark the start of flight training. Pair it with a note about the journey ahead, rather than filling in any flight-record pages yourself.

    What to know: Check with their instructor first: they may already have a logbook or use a different format.

    Product details & source ↗
  7. 7
    A little holiday aviation

    Blue Angels jet ornament

    Listed price: $17.99 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A small nod to a favorite airshow team. Add it to a larger gift, or make it the start of an aviation ornament tradition.

    What to know: Best for a Blue Angels fan; a favorite aircraft or team makes a small gift feel personal.

    Product details & source ↗
  8. 8
    Off-duty aviation

    Cessna patch trucker cap

    Listed price: $34.99 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A casual option for the Cessna enthusiast who already owns the flight gear they need. The navy-and-scarlet color scheme makes it easy to wear away from the airport.

    What to know: Confirm they like caps and Cessna; a familiar logo is more personal than a random airplane.

    Product details & source ↗
  9. 9
    For the organized pilot

    Flight Gear rotating kneeboard

    Listed price: $22.95 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A practical way to keep a compatible iPad in reach. It is most useful when you already know the pilot wants a kneeboard rather than a mounted tablet.

    What to know: Confirm the exact iPad model, case and preferred cockpit setup with the retailer.

    Product details & source ↗
  10. 10
    A small travel upgrade

    Pro Crew luggage tag

    Listed price: $9.99 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A low-cost gift for a working pilot’s luggage. It is especially easy to combine with a card or another small item when you want something useful to unwrap.

    What to know: A CREW tag is a bag accessory, not airport identification or an access credential.

    Product details & source ↗

Not a pilot? No problem.

Four checks to make before you buy an aviation gift.

Read the buying checklist ›
  1. Find the personal connection. Their first airplane, favorite airshow, or an item they actually asked for.
  2. Check the fit. Aircraft plugs, tablet models, clothing sizes and shelf space all matter.
  3. Check the delivered total. Include tax and shipping, then read the delivery estimate and return terms.
  4. Keep technical gifts collaborative. For headsets and cockpit equipment, let the pilot choose the exact version.
